subject: tie/tied/untie: bareword class name must use the bless class-name mechanism, not a global bareword rule
description:
t/op/avhv.t:114 `tie %fake, Tie::StdHash;` — a BAREWORD class — compiles to a call and dies (`undef-fn:Tie::pl-StdHash`). Quoted `tie @a, 'Tie::StdArray'` works, and Tie::StdHash itself loads fine from the system @INC.

DECIDED s317 (Fable, fable-answers-s316v.md §1): the bless route below is APPROVED and W1-eligible. Execute it now. Required probe battery = the three killers from the failed attempts: `my $a = Foo::init` (must stay a call), `Count::DATA->getline` (must keep p-resolve-invocant), quoted-vs-bareword tie. Full quadruple. The GENERAL bareword rule stays untouched until E5.0 (task #153).

DO NOT widen PExpr's `_bareword_string` rule. Three attempts in s316v, all reverted; tree never carried any of them:

1. Any qualified bareword with no `has_prototype` → string. BROKE `package Foo; sub init` + `my $a = Foo::init` (perl CALLED, PCL "Foo::init"). Silent call→string.
2. Added the two facts that make the rule sound (user pointed at both, both already tracked):
   - `strict_subs` (Environment::has_pragma) — under `use strict` an undeclared bareword here is a COMPILE ERROR, so by principle 9 anything that compiles in strict code is a declared call; the rule must never fire under strict. (Attempt 1's core defect was OR-ing outside that branch.)
   - `declared_subs` ({name, package}) is the PACKAGE-QUALIFIED oracle `has_prototype` cannot be: `package Foo; sub init` stores name=init/package=Foo, so "$pkg::$name" answers the `Foo::init` query. Parser2:734 already documents declared_subs as the bareword-vs-string oracle.
   Probes all matched — but corpus-diff caught method.t: the method INVOCANT `Count::DATA->getline` lost its `(p-resolve-invocant …)` wrapper, hard-wiring the class and deleting perl's runtime class-vs-filehandle resolution. Those are method.t's "file handles take priority" rows. Invisible to a probe, because with no filehandle present both answers agree.
3. Guarded on "next token is `->`". NO EFFECT — method.t still stringified, so the arrow is not at $e->[$i+1] in that path. The invocant reaches this decision by a route not yet understood.

CORRECT APPROACH (approved, and it never touches the global rule): `bless` already has a class-name-bareword branch (Pl/ExprToCL.pm ~2007, `$is_bareword`). `tie`/`tied`/`untie` take a class name in exactly that argument position — route them through the SAME mechanism (CLAUDE.md 11). That is a per-builtin argument-position rule, so it cannot reach `Foo::init` or a method invocant at all.

If the general rule is ever wanted, prerequisites: (a) understand how a method invocant reaches PExpr:3695 and exclude it structurally (E5.0 / Option B territory); (b) position-aware sub declarations (perl strings a sub declared LATER; PCL's declared_subs is a whole-file pre-pass, so `my $r = Foo::later;` gives "Foo::later" in perl vs a call in PCL).

Probes: scratchpad w0/t1-t6.pl, s1-s3.pl.
activeForm: Routing tie/tied/untie bareword class through the bless mechanism
